name: Azbuk
overview: Azbuk was a male official of the district of Beth-zur mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is noted primarily for his administrative role within this region during the post-exilic period. Beyond his official capacity, no further tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Azbuk is a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 3:16. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to the name in the biblical text, and it is presented plainly without additional titles or meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Azbuk as the father of Nehemiah, indicating a direct familial connection to this significant biblical figure. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this father-son link.
scriptureSignificance: Azbuk's significance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his role as an official in Beth-zur and as the father of Nehemiah, a key leader in the restoration of Jerusalem. His mention underscores the administrative structure supporting the rebuilding efforts and highlights the lineage of Nehemiah, connecting him to established leadership within the community. Though Azbuk himself is not the focus of extensive narrative, his position and relationship contribute to the historical and spiritual context of the post-exilic restoration.
